transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Recording id: ff-20250915-7b3c-ldv
Attendees: Jordan Marks (Redwood AE), Sofia Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Alves (Redwood Solutions), Maya Patel (Aurelia ML), Ethan Ross (Aurelia Platform), Sara Ling (Aurelia PM), Tom Bauer (Aurelia Security), Luis Ortega (Aurelia SRE)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- POC scoping focused on benchmark planning and onboarding customer load scripts.
- Decisions: start with 2-week sandbox dedicated run, capture streaming and non-streaming profiles, validate P95 latency and tokens/sec.
- Next steps: share adapter template, customer to provide traces, Redwood to run baseline tests.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can we get names?
[00:05] Maya: Maya Patel here, ML lead.
[00:07] Ethan: Ethan Ross, platform.
[00:09] Sara: Sara Ling, product.
[00:11] Tom: Tom Bauer, security.
[00:13] Luis: Luis Ortega, SRE.
[00:15] Jordan: Great, from Redwood Sofia the SE and Diego in solutions. Today's goal is to scope the benchmark run — what scripts you have, streaming vs non-streaming, success criteria, and timeline.
[00:28] Sofia: I'll focus on the harness integration details — adapter expectations, payload shapes, and metrics we collect. We'll also talk about where KV cache and prefix caching might change numbers for you.
[00:40] Maya: Quick background — we're building a clinical triage assistant that summarizes notes and produces structured recommendations. Typical input sizes vary a lot; median ~450 tokens, tail to ~3k. We also do a small embedding flow for similarity search.
[00:55] Ethan: Our infra currently uses a mix of async batch jobs and near-real-time streaming endpoints. For this POC we want to validate both: 1) non-streaming batch throughput for bulk transforms, and 2) streaming low-latency responses for interactive UI.
[01:10] Jordan: Okay good. Two axes. For success criteria, what are your thresholds?
[01:15] Sara: From product: P95 under 400ms for interactive flows, and for batch we want cost < $0.0007 per 1k tokens processed — rough target.
[01:25] Tom: Security-wise we need to confirm data residency for PHI-adjacent data and KMS integration. We'll treat the trace as anonymized but need to know retention and audit logging.
[01:40] Diego: Noted. For the harness, we typically ask for: sample payloads, a 1-hour high-fidelity traffic trace (anonymized), and a token distribution histogram. We'll provide an adapter template in Node/Python to map your payload shape to the harness.
[01:55] Ethan: We can give a gzipped trace — events with timestamps and session ids. Also need to make sure there's no PII.
[02:01] Sofia: That's fine. Adapter expectations: the harness will call into model endpoint with either streaming websocket or non-streaming HTTP post. We support both modes. For streaming tests we can replay event-by-event and keep KV cache between consecutive tokens when appropriate. For non-streaming, we run batched requests.
[02:20] Maya: How do you simulate user think time for streaming? That's important for realistic concurrency.
[02:23] Sofia: We have a delay model you can configure — think time distribution per session, ramp-up, steady-state, and burst phases. We'll want to know your expected concurrent sessions and average tokens per session.
[02:35] Sara: Our product expects 150 concurrent interactive users at peak with bursts to 400 for ~2 minutes. Average tokens per response ~650, with multi-turn context sometimes 2-3 messages.
[02:46] Jordan: Good — those numbers help size the Dedicated sandbox. Diego, does that fit a 4xA10 pool or do we need denser GPUs?
[02:53] Diego: Initial estimate: for 150 concurrent low-latency streams with 650 tokens per response and model ~13B FP16, that maps to roughly 6–8 GPUs if we aim for P95 350–450ms. If you want strict 200ms we'd push to higher throughput hardware or more aggressive quantization. We'll provide a more detailed table after Sofia runs baseline.
[03:12] Ethan: For batch, our nightly job processes ~2 million documents averaging 800 tokens each — that's heavy. We mainly care about cost-per-token and total window to finish within maintenance window (2 hours).
[03:25] Sofia: For batch throughput we will test streaming disabled, larger batch sizes, and measure tokens/sec and cost. For your maintenance window target, we will run a multi-GPU parallel batch test. Please provide a sample of the largest documents to check sequence length impact.
[03:40] Tom: On encryption: we require customer-managed KMS keys for any persisted cache or logs that include derived outputs. Is that supported in the private/dedicated offering?
[03:50] Jordan: Yes — Dedicated and Private both support KMS/HSM integration; we'll surface the specific controls relevant to your deployment. We'll also share SOC2 + audit artifacts.
[04:02] Maya: One question — how do you handle prefix caching and KV cache effects between streaming and non-streaming runs when comparing apples-to-apples?
[04:08] Sofia: Good call. For apples-to-apples we run two baseline modes: cold start (no cache), and warm start (seeded cache from a replay of representative traffic). We'll report both P95 and tokens/sec. Warm cache is closer to production for interactive flows.
[04:22] Luis: We need telemetry — per-request trace ids, token-level timing, GPU utilization, and memory pressure alerts. Can those be emitted from the harness?
[04:30] Diego: Yes — harness ships with a telemetry collector. We'll send per-request timings (queue, compute, stream chunk latency), GPU metrics, and a CSV/TSV export you can ingest. We can also instrument with your Prometheus endpoints if you want.
[04:43] Sara: About the script adapter: will you accept a node script that pulls from our trace and maps fields?
[04:48] Sofia: Absolutely. We'll send a Python and Node template. Key requirements: idempotent replay, ability to emulate think time, flag to toggle streaming vs non-streaming, and a mode to inject network jitter.
[04:59] Ethan: What's the suggested timeline? We have an internal deadline end of October to decide vendor for production.
[05:04] Jordan: Proposal: this week we exchange artifacts, next week Redwood provisions a 2-week dedicated sandbox and runs baseline tests (hosted vs dedicated), and week after we iterate on script tuning and run full validation. That lands final report early October.
[05:18] Maya: That sounds tight but doable. We need to align calendar — Sara will coordinate.
[05:22] Sara: I'll send calendar invites for the provisioning window and a follow-up on script onboarding.
[05:26] Tom: A couple of security caveats: any persistent logs retained on Redwood side must be configurable for 0 retention, and we need export controls documented for EU data.
[05:36] Jordan: We'll add those to the security pack. Diego — can you sketch a test matrix quickly?
[05:40] Diego: Sure. High-level test matrix I propose (I'll follow up in doc):
- Mode A: Non-streaming bulk runs, batch sizes [1k, 5k, 10k tokens] across 1,2,4,8 GPUs. Measure total time, tokens/sec, cost.
- Mode B: Streaming interactive runs, concurrency [50,150,400], think-time distributions (p10,p50,p90), warm vs cold cache. Measure P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and failed requests.
- Mode C: Mixed (embedding + generation) pipeline runs to validate multi-workload interference.

[06:10] Maya: For warm cache seeding, do you need a separate run or can you seed it with a short replay beforehand?
[06:15] Sofia: Short replay is sufficient. We'll include that as a pre-step in the harness.
[06:20] Ethan: Regarding cost targets — Sara's number was $0.0007 per 1k tokens. How realistic is that?
[06:25] Diego: Depends on model family and quantization. If you can accept an 8-bit quantized variant, cost drops considerably. We'll include model variants in the matrix: 7B/13B/13B-quantized.
[06:40] Tom: We'll need to ensure that quantization doesn't break QA/regulatory outputs. We expect Redwood to help run QA evals on prompt-sets.
[06:47] Sofia: We can run eval harnesses against your prompt sets and surface regressions; that's part of Redwood Optimize. Please attach a representative prompt set.
[06:55] Sara: We'll compile a set of ~200 prompts covering clinical, edge cases, and hallucination checks.
[07:02] Jordan: Great. A few pragmatic notes: 1) we'll provide a Docker-based harness runner so you can run locally, 2) we'll maintain a shared spreadsheet for results, and 3) expect an initial findings deck after the first week of tests.
[07:18] Luis: Can we get the harness to emit per-token cost estimates inline so we can map cost to query types?
[07:23] Diego: Yes, we'll add per-request token accounting to the telemetry export.
[07:27] Maya: One more: for streaming we sometimes have partial responses that then finish. Do you charge for partial tokens?
[07:33] Jordan: Our billing is based on consumed tokens; for the POC we'll show raw token counts and a modeled cost so you can decide billing semantics later.
[07:40] Sara: Anything else on legal/procurement?
[07:42] Tom: We'll need an NDA amendment to cover trace data and explicit terms for sandbox access.
[07:48] Jordan: Noted — legal will follow up.
[07:52] Sofia: Action item recap: we'll send adapter templates, sketch the test matrix, and run a short baseline next week. Customer will provide traces, prompt sets, and security constraints.
[08:05] Jordan: Perfect. Let's recap next steps and owners. (recap enumerated)
[08:20] Maya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to seeing the initial baseline.
[08:23] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up by EOD with the templates.
